item.text: I’ve finished the API surface plan and I’m moving into file creation now. The implementation is going to centralize most behavior in shared core modules and use thin compatibility wrappers for the many documented import paths, so the package stays broad without becoming unmaintainable.

I’m laying down the packaging/config/utilities layer first because most of the later modules depend on it. After this patch I can wire the analysis and rendering stacks against stable settings and helper APIs instead of threading ad hoc state through the package.

I’ve got the packaging and settings layer in place. The next patch is the analysis core itself: type inference, statistical summaries, duplicates, correlations, missing-data summaries, alerts, and the raw `BaseDescription` object that `ProfileReport` will sit on top of.

The analysis layer is in place, but it depends on plotting helpers for histograms, missing-value diagrams, correlations, and time-series visuals. I’m wiring those next so the report pipeline can actually render its outputs instead of only computing raw summaries.

The next layer is the presentation model: generic renderable objects plus HTML/widget flavours. I’m keeping the public module layout compatible, but the implementation itself is centralized so the surface stays wide while the logic stays maintainable.

The remaining pieces are the report assembly functions and the public `ProfileReport`/`compare` API. I’m wiring those now so the statistical description, renderable tree, and export paths line up end to end instead of staying as separate subsystems.

The raw renderer tree is done. I’m now stitching the compatibility surface around it: `ProfileReport`, `compare`, serialization, pandas monkeypatching, CLI, and the deep legacy module paths the real package exposes.

I’ve completed the compatibility surface, and I’m switching to verification now. This phase is mostly import and syntax cleanup: the project is broad enough at this point that a compile pass will catch the hidden integration mistakes faster than reading files by hand.
